chapter_title: Concerning the Man who is ugly in his Body, [but] beautiful [in his Soul].
chapter_note: Most of the chapter is hagiographic scene-setting (Mani in a public assembly) plus moral admonition culminating in an explicit Gospel saying (NT overlay). The oldest recoverable teaching layer here is concentrated in the impersonal, technical exposition of pearl formation (¶9–14, with a dialogue-attribution stripped in ¶9) and the cosmological return/rest of liberated souls (¶17). The later editor then applies the pearl imagery to the holy church and apostles (¶15–16) and ends with direct exhortation (¶18).

paragraphs.temporal_note: Narrative scene-setting with ‘the apostle’ in a public gathering; hagiographic/compilational framing rather than teaching exposition.
Continues the narrative portrait of an elect man; institutional descriptors (‘elect’, ‘commandments’) function as story apparatus, not systematic cosmological teaching.
Congregational reaction scene (mocking, scoffing) in narrative voice; not a cosmological/correspondential mapping layer.
Hagiographic action (embrace/kiss) featuring ‘the glorious one’/‘apostle’; typical editorial story-frame.
Dialogue lead-in (‘He says to them:’) attached to the public assembly setting; a framing hinge rather than core exposition.

Moral admonition anchored to a Gospel-style authority claim (‘For the saviour says…’) and a ‘least of the faithful/angel sees the face of the Father’ motif (NT entry vector). Even where it uses inner/outer man language, the paragraph’s climactic warrant is Gospel-citation overlay.
Narrative transition describing the audience response and seating; part of the chapter’s hagiographic container.
Formal disciple question (‘Tell us, our master…’) is a classic Kephalaia Q&A frame device introducing the next teaching block.

paragraphs.core_text: “Pearls shall arise not in every place in the sea, nor be formed in the sea as a whole. Rather, in various places that are in this sea, pearls are formed in them [ ... ... ] that sea, in which the [pearls] shall be formed [ ... ] this [ ... ... ] what the sea shall [ ... ... ] its fire above and comes [down ... ... ] and it makes foam like the drop of water that flows [ ... ] down in rainwater [ ... ] is the water [ ... ... d]own first [ ... ... ] foam and comes down [ ... ... ] the sweet waters [ ... ... ] the waters.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed dialogue-attribution/frame formula (‘+The enlightener says to them:+’) and page marker (‘⟨p.203⟩’) as later compilational wrapping around an expository teaching unit.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Underlying content is impersonal, technical explanation (how pearls form) without ecclesial address; but it is introduced by a compilational dialogue-attribution that must be stripped.

paragraphs.core_text: “This drop of water shall [ ... ] down to the sweet waters and [ ... ] and they absorbed them and were combined with the [ ... ]. They did not [d]escend to the depths of the sea, but they [ ... ... ] it floated on the surface of the waters [ ... ... ] to it. The foam and the pearl-shell shall be formed [ ... ] this wholesome drop [ ... ... ] it, and it becomes a pe[arl ... ] that makes a drop of rainwater [ ... ] waters [ ... ] it not being whole. It breaks and separates out into many droplets, and it has time to become a drop of sweet water [ ... ] and comes up in the sea of [ ... ] rain and sweet water; and it is accomodated in the shell, which at first is foam. They shall be joined with each other at [this] time, and are shaped and become a great pea[r]l, a great and valued kind.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Extended, stepwise process-description in an impersonal explanatory voice; no institutional identification or citation formula.

paragraphs.core_text: “When, however, a drop of rainwater falls, and that drop breaks into many droplets and various , they shall be formed into and be confined in [n]umerous pearls, in the shell and the pearl-shell. One might form two pearls, another may form three, others may form five; some mould more than these, some fewer.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Systematic numerical variation within the process account; remains within the descriptive ‘how it is formed’ register (no application to church/audience).

paragraphs.core_text: “Now, when you might [find a] whole drop, and the shell receives it, it shall become a great and valued [pe]arl as its worth is perfected. [However], if these two droplets will have time (to adhere) to one another before any (water particle) escapes, and they mix with e[ach o]ther, and the shell [ ... ] before they break into [ ... ] within [ ... ] in a great kind [ ... ... ] the drop of rain, which [ ... ... ] another one, that [ ... ... ] the [w]aters form them in [ ... and] in a great, valued commodity.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Continues the technical formation account with conditional cases (whole drop vs. mixed droplets); still non-institutional exposition.

paragraphs.core_text: “Behold, [I, I have] taught you how sea-pearls shall be formed. I have told you that as a pearl shall come into existence by means of rainwater that has [ti]me to become foam, the pearl-shell shall come into existence by means of the foam, and the foam itself comes into being by means of the transformation and the [ ... ] of the sea.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Summative closure of the process-teaching; first-person recap, but still within the same impersonal instructional register (no ecclesial mapping yet).

paragraphs.core_text: “Then immediately at the time when [ ... ... ] the pearl divers know it, they shall [ ... ] and they [ ... d]own to those places and they bring pearls up from the depths of the sea, and each pearl diver finds according to the fortune that is [ordai]ned for him. The pearl divers shall [gi]ve them to the traders, and the traders give them to the kings and the nobles.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Parabolic narrative mechanics (divers → traders → kings/nobles) still stated within the imagery itself, prior to overt ecclesial identification.
Explicit institutional application (‘This is also what the holy church is like’) crosses from image-system into community identity; classic cosmos/image → church-pointing move.

Continues ecclesial application (‘apostles are like the divers’) even while naming cosmic terms (‘light-givers’, ‘aeons’); the paragraph’s function is institutional mapping, so it belongs to the pastoral/application layer.

paragraphs.core_text: “Fo[r a]ll the souls that ascend in the flesh of mankind and are freed shall be brought back to the great aeons of light. A place of rest comes about for them, at that place in the aeons of greatness.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Returns to impersonal cosmological-soteriological mechanism (souls freed → brought back to Aeons of Light → rest place), without direct church/audience address.
Direct second-person exhortation (‘You too, my beloved ones, struggle…’) and imperative application voice; explicitly pastoral closing appeal.
